settings.name: a found browser
settings.paneHtml:
Browser for the coding agent
With this on, the agent on the Code page can open a web page in a real browser (Chrome, Chromium, Edge or Brave on this computer), read it, click, type, scroll and take screenshots, for example to test the app it is building on a local dev server. You see the same page live in the Browser panel of the Code page and can take over, or leave comments on elements. Every browser action asks first, like the other network tools. It is off until you turn it on.
How it runs
Off: the browser runs without a window (headless) and you watch it in the panel. On: a real window opens on this computer, for example to log in to a site once. Needs a display (not for servers and containers).
The browser uses its own profile folder inside fLLM's data folder, never the profile of your own browser. Off: every start uses a fresh, throw-away profile.
Addresses on this computer or your network can hold things that must not be reached by accident, so they are refused unless allowed here. Link-local and cloud-metadata addresses (169.254.x.x) are never reachable. A page from the internet can never load local addresses, whatever you choose.
A path or a program name. The environment variable FLLM_BROWSER wins over this field.
Safety
Only http and https pages can be opened (no files, no browser-internal pages). Downloads, camera, microphone, location and notifications are refused. The agent's browser can hold logged-in sessions, so its controls are only reachable from this computer, even when the server has an API key. If you log in to a site in the shown window, the agent can use that session: only do it for sites you are willing to let the agent act on.
